headline: Depardieu will stand trial for rape. She spoke up in 2018.
summary: A Paris appeals court ruled Thursday that Gérard Depardieu, 77, must stand trial for raping and sexually assaulting actress Charlotte Arnould at his home in August 2018. She was 22 and reported it days later. He denies it. Two weeks ago he dropped his appeal of a separate conviction for assaulting two women on a film set, and apologised.
cover_answer: Both sides tell a court what happened. Then it decides.
table_question: Should fame count for anything in a courtroom?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A famous actor from France, a man named Gérard Depardieu, is accused of hurting a woman, and a court said he has to go to trial. He is 77, old enough to be a great-grandpa. A trial is where grown-ups in a court listen to both sides and decide what is true. The judges have it, and you are safe.
5-7.why: Only if they hear it. 'Hurting a woman' is true and enough. The trial is the thing to explain, and it ends with the judges holding it.
5-7.why_long: Nothing to raise with a five-year-old. This is for the child who hears the name on the radio. They take one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them none: 'hurting a woman' is true and stops there, and the trial, grown-ups listening to both sides, is what gets explained. Expect 'is he in jail?' No. A trial comes first.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: In 2018 an actress said Gérard Depardieu, a huge French film star, raped her at his home. The case was dropped for lack of evidence. She filed her own complaint, a judge investigated, and on Thursday a court ordered a trial. A referee going back to the tape.
8-12.why: Dates and steps, and the question they already ask: one rulebook for a star?
8-12.why_long: A child this age is working out rules and whether adults apply them to everyone. The chain is dates and steps: an accusation, a dropped case, her own complaint, an investigation, a trial order eight years on. The referee going back to the tape is the mechanism. Expect 'is he guilty?' Nobody knows yet. That is what the trial is for.

13-17.script: Does fame buy a fairer trial, or a harsher one? Depardieu dominated French film for 50 years. On Thursday a court sent him to trial for raping Charlotte Arnould in 2018, which he denies. Two weeks ago he dropped an appeal of a separate assault conviction and apologised. Does one case colour the other?
13-17.why: One denied, one admitted. They can hold both and still owe him a trial.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: he admitted assaulting two women on a set, and he is presumed innocent of this charge until a court rules. The script hands them that pair and asks whether one apology should colour the other case. Expect 'why did Macron defend him?' Presumption of innocence, he said. Women's groups objected.

5-7.a: A day in court where both sides tell what happened and judges decide. It is how grown-ups settle a serious accusation.

8-12.q: Why did it take eight years?
8-12.a: Dropped for lack of evidence at first. Her own complaint reopened it in 2020.
Nobody knows yet. That is what the trial decides. He denies it.

13-17.a: In 2023 he said Depardieu 'makes France proud' and cited the presumption of innocence.

13-17.q: Can he still be found not guilty?
13-17.a: Yes. A trial order is not a verdict. He denies it and may appeal.
